MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a multiple of 6? (1 mark)
   A. 54
   B. 56
   C. 55
   D. 53

2. In the number 7,958, the digit 9 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Tens
   B. Thousands
   C. Hundreds
   D. Ones

3. What is the total value of the digit 3 in 5,306? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 300
   C. 3,000
   D. 30

4. Round 995 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 900
   B. 1010
   C. 990
   D. 1000

5. Which Roman numeral stands for 4? (1 mark)
   A. IV
   B. VX
   C. VIIII
   D. IIII

6. Why can we add 3,875 + 2,450 in either order? (1 mark)
   A. The sum changes when the order changes
   B. The sum stays the same when numbers are added in any order
   C. The answer is always the bigger number
   D. Only the bigger number can go first

7. A tank held 8,000 litres of water. The school used 3,450 litres. How many litres are left? (1 mark)
   A. 4,550 litres
   B. 4,540 litres
   C. 5,450 litres
   D. 4,650 litres

8. A farmer had 6,500 seedlings and planted 2,875 of them. How many seedlings are left? (1 mark)
   A. 4,375 seedlings
   B. 3,725 seedlings
   C. 3,615 seedlings
   D. 3,625 seedlings

9. What is the next number in the pattern 800, 675, 550, 425, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 675
   B. 425
   C. 300
   D. 175

10. What is the next number in the pattern 5,000, 4,750, 4,500, 4,250, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 4,250
   B. 4,000
   C. 4,750
   D. 3,750

11. In 5,432 − 2,718, the ones digit 2 is smaller than 8. From which digit do we borrow? (1 mark)
   A. We swap the 2 and the 8
   B. The thousands digit 5, which becomes 4
   C. The hundreds digit 4, which becomes 3
   D. The tens digit 3, which becomes 2

12. What is 45 × 20? (1 mark)
   A. 900
   B. 9,000
   C. 90
   D. 65

13. A book costs Ksh 45. How much do 24 books cost? (1 mark)
   A. 1,180 shillings
   B. 1,080 shillings
   C. 1,060 shillings
   D. 1,070 shillings

14. A jerrycan holds 20 litres. How many litres do 100 jerrycans hold? (1 mark)
   A. 1,980 litres
   B. 2,000 litres
   C. 1,990 litres
   D. 2,100 litres

15. Estimate 19 × 31 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 600
   B. 500
   C. 700
   D. 6,000

16. Which division fact belongs to the same family as 8 × 3 = 24? (1 mark)
   A. 24 ÷ 8 = 3
   B. 3 ÷ 8 = 24
   C. 24 ÷ 24 = 8
   D. 24 ÷ 8 = 8

17. Change 11/4 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 3 2/4
   B. 3 3/4
   C. 2 4/4
   D. 2 3/4

18. Write 0.8 as a fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 1/8
   B. 80/10
   C. 8/10
   D. 8/100

19. In the number 5.68, the digit 6 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Ones
   B. Tenths
   C. Tens
   D. Hundredths

20. A hundred square has 7 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 0.07
   C. 0.7
   D. 0.007

21. Which is the largest number: 2.5, 2.05, 2.55, 2.505? (1 mark)
   A. 2.55
   B. 2.505
   C. 2.5
   D. 2.05

22. What is 5 m 20 cm − 2 m 75 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 3 m 45 cm
   B. 2 m 45 cm
   C. 2 m 55 cm
   D. 2 m 35 cm

23. Change 908 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 10 m 8 cm
   B. 90 cm
   C. 9 m 8 cm
   D. 9 m 58 cm

24. A rectangle is made of 7 rows with 9 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 32 square units
   B. 63 square units
   C. 16 square units
   D. 70 square units

25. A rectangle is made of 8 rows with 12 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 40 square units
   B. 104 square units
   C. 96 square units
   D. 20 square units

26. A rectangle is made of 9 rows with 4 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 26 square units
   B. 45 square units
   C. 36 square units
   D. 13 square units

27. A rectangle is made of 12 rows with 7 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 96 square units
   B. 84 square units
   C. 19 square units
   D. 38 square units

28. A cuboid has a volume of 100 blocks. One layer has 20 blocks. How many layers are there? (1 mark)
   A. 120
   B. 5
   C. 80
   D. 6

29. A cuboid is 5 blocks long, 2 blocks wide and 3 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 35 blocks
   B. 30 blocks
   C. 28 blocks
   D. 10 blocks

30. How many half-litre containers fill 1 litre? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 4
   C. 3
   D. 2

31. How many 1/4 L cups can be filled from 3 L of milk? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 9
   C. 6
   D. 7

32. What is 4 kg − 1/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 4 1/4 kg
   B. 4 kg
   C. 3 3/4 kg
   D. 3 1/2 kg

33. What is 1 3/4 kg + 2 1/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 4 1/2 kg
   B. 4 1/4 kg
   C. 4 kg
   D. 3 3/4 kg

34. Achieng buys 3 packets of flour of 1/2 kg each and 2 packets of sugar of 1 kg each. What is the total mass? (1 mark)
   A. 3 kg
   B. 2 1/2 kg
   C. 3 1/2 kg
   D. 5 kg

35. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 2 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 3. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 2:03
   B. 3:15
   C. 2:15
   D. 2:45

36. How many minutes are in 3 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 240 minutes
   B. 300 minutes
   C. 72 minutes
   D. 180 minutes

37. One unit costs Ksh 45. What is the cost of 5 mandazi? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 235
   B. Ksh 50
   C. Ksh 225
   D. Ksh 180

38. A customer pays with Ksh 500 for goods that cost Ksh 235. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 265
   B. Ksh 735
   C. Ksh 365
   D. Ksh 255

39. Which shape has no corners? (1 mark)
   A. Rectangle
   B. Circle
   C. Square
   D. Triangle

40. The table shows the pets kept by 10 families: dog 3, cat 3, rabbit 2, hen 2. How many are dog or hen together? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 5
   C. 3
   D. 4

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Change Ksh 12 to cents and 1,250 cents to shillings. (2 marks)

42. Wanjiru studied for 1 hour 20 minutes on Monday and 45 minutes on Tuesday. How long did she study in all? (3 marks)

43. Find and name three objects in the classroom that show a rectangle, a circle and a triangle. (3 marks)

44. A tanker fills 100 jerrycans of 20 litres each. How many litres is that? (2 marks)

45. A school tank held 8,500 litres of water. The school used 3,275 litres in the first week and 1,850 litres in the second week. How much water is left? Check your answer. (5 marks)

46. Describe how you can use a folded piece of paper to test whether a corner is a right angle. (3 marks)

47. Explain how you can use addition to check a subtraction. Use 7,865 − 3,542 = 4,323 as an example. (3 marks)

48. A trader buys 18 crates with 35 bananas in each crate. How many bananas are there altogether? (3 marks)

49. A shopkeeper counts up to give change. A customer buys goods for Ksh 750 and pays with Ksh 1,000. Show how the shopkeeper counts up. (3 marks)

50. Mama Njoki has 24 oranges. She gives 3/8 of them to her neighbours and 1/4 of them to a friend. (a) How many oranges does she give to her neighbours? (b) How many does she give to her friend? (c) How many oranges are left? (5 marks)

51. Give two things you should do to stay safe when you collect data about vehicles. (2 marks)

52. A rectangular plot is 12 m long and 8 m wide. Peter walks once round the plot. How far does he walk? (3 marks)

53. Add 3,568 and 2,276 and say how many times you regrouped. (3 marks)

54. Simplify 2a + 5 + 3a + 1 and find its value when a = 4. (4 marks)

55. Write the four facts that belong to an array of 3 rows with 8 dots in each row. (4 marks)

56. Add 2 1/2 kg and 1 3/4 kg. Show your working. (3 marks)

57. Change 45/100, 6/100 and 7/10 into decimals. (3 marks)

58. Change 2 1/3 and 1 5/6 to improper fractions. (4 marks)

59. Explain the difference between area and volume. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 54
   54 = 6 × 9, so 54 is a multiple of 6.

2. C — Hundreds
   Counting from the right the places are ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands. The digit 9 is in the hundreds place.

3. B — 300
   The digit 3 is in the hundreds place, so its total value is 3 × 100 = 300.

4. D — 1000
   Look at the ones digit 5. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 995 rounds to 1000.

5. A — IV
   4 is written IV. I before V is 5 − 1.

6. B — The sum stays the same when numbers are added in any order
   Addition can be done in any order: 3,875 + 2,450 = 2,450 + 3,875 = 6,325.

7. A — 4,550 litres
   Subtract 8,000 − 3,450 = 4,550. Check by adding: 4,550 + 3,450 = 8,000.

8. D — 3,625 seedlings
   Subtract 6,500 − 2,875 = 3,625. Check by adding: 3,625 + 2,875 = 6,500.

9. C — 300
   The rule is subtract 125. 425 − 125 = 300.

10. B — 4,000
   The rule is subtract 250. 4,250 − 250 = 4,000.

11. D — The tens digit 3, which becomes 2
   Borrow one ten from the tens column. The 3 becomes 2 and the ones digit 2 becomes 12.

12. A — 900
   45 × 2 = 90, then × 10 gives 900.

13. B — 1,080 shillings
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 1,080 shillings.

14. B — 2,000 litres
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 2,000 litres.

15. A — 600
   19 rounds to 20 and 31 rounds to 30. 20 × 30 = 600.

16. A — 24 ÷ 8 = 3
   Division undoes multiplication. Since 8 × 3 = 24, we know 24 ÷ 8 = 3 and 24 ÷ 3 = 8.

17. D — 2 3/4
   11 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 3. The whole number is 2 and the fraction is 3/4, so 11/4 = 2 3/4.

18. C — 8/10
   The last digit of 0.8 is in the tenths place, so the denominator is 10. 0.8 = 8/10.

19. B — Tenths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 5.68 the digit 6 is in the tenths place.

20. B — 0.07
   7 out of 100 squares is 7/100 = 0.07.

21. A — 2.55
   Give every number the same number of decimal places and compare from the left. The largest number is 2.55.

22. B — 2 m 45 cm
   520 − 275 = 245 cm = 2 m 45 cm.

23. C — 9 m 8 cm
   908 ÷ 100 = 9 remainder 8. So 908 cm = 9 m 8 cm.

24. B — 63 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 7 × 9 = 63 square units.

25. C — 96 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 8 × 12 = 96 square units.

26. C — 36 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 9 × 4 = 36 square units.

27. B — 84 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 12 × 7 = 84 square units.

28. B — 5
   Layers = 100 ÷ 20 = 5.

29. B — 30 blocks
   One layer has 5 × 2 = 10 blocks. There are 3 layers, so the volume is 10 × 3 = 30 blocks.

30. D — 2
   Two halves make one whole.

31. A — 12
   Each litre fills 4 cups, so 3 L fills 3 × 4 = 12 cups.

32. C — 3 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 4 kg − 1/4 kg = 3 3/4 kg.

33. C — 4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 1 3/4 kg + 2 1/4 kg = 4 kg.

34. C — 3 1/2 kg
   3 × 1/2 = 1 1/2 kg and 2 × 1 = 2 kg. 1 1/2 + 2 = 3 1/2 kg.

35. C — 2:15
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 3 shows 3 × 5 = 15 minutes, so the time is 2:15.

36. D — 180 minutes
   1 hour = 60 minutes, so 3 × 60 = 180 minutes.

37. C — Ksh 225
   Cost = number × price = 5 × 45 = Ksh 225.

38. A — Ksh 265
   Change = amount paid − cost = 500 − 235 = Ksh 265.

39. B — Circle
   A circle has one curved edge and no corners.

40. B — 5
   3 + 2 = 5.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 12 = 1,200 cents; 1,250 cents = Ksh 12.50
   Working / marking points: 12 × 100 = 1,200 (1 mark); 1,250 ÷ 100 = 12 remainder 50, so Ksh 12.50 (1 mark).

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 hours 5 minutes
   Working / marking points: 20 + 45 = 65 min (1 mark); 1 h + 65 min = 2 h 5 min (2 marks).

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example a blackboard (rectangle), a clock face (circle) and a set square (triangle).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct object matched to a shape.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: 2,000 litres
   Working / marking points: 20 × 100 = 2,000. 1 mark for the multiplication and 1 mark for units.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: 3,375 litres
   Working / marking points: 8,500 − 3,275 = 5,225 (2 marks); 5,225 − 1,850 = 3,375 (2 marks); check by adding 3,375 + 1,850 + 3,275 = 8,500 (1 mark).

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fold a paper twice to make a neat square corner. Place its corner on the corner of the object. If it fits exactly, the corner is a right angle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for folding to make a square corner, 1 mark for placing it on the corner, 1 mark for saying it fits exactly.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Add the answer to the number that was taken away: 4,323 + 3,542 = 7,865, which is the starting number, so the subtraction is correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying add the answer and the smaller number, 1 mark for the example, 1 mark for saying the result matches the starting number.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: 630 bananas
   Working / marking points: 18 × 5 = 90 (1 mark); 18 × 30 = 540 (1 mark); 90 + 540 = 630 (1 mark).

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: From 750 to 800 is 50, and from 800 to 1,000 is 200. Change = 50 + 200 = Ksh 250.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for counting to 800, 1 mark for counting to 1,000, 1 mark for adding to make Ksh 250.

50. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 9 oranges (b) 6 oranges (c) 9 oranges
   Working / marking points: (a) 24 ÷ 8 = 3, 3 × 3 = 9 (2 marks); (b) 24 ÷ 4 = 6 (1 mark); (c) 24 − 9 − 6 = 9 (2 marks).

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Count from a safe place inside the school gate and stay with a teacher. Do not stand in or near the road.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible safety rule.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: 40 m
   Working / marking points: 12 + 8 + 12 + 8 = 40 m. 1 mark for identifying perimeter, 1 mark for the sum, 1 mark for unit.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: 5,844. You regrouped twice (ones to tens, tens to hundreds).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the correct sum, 1 mark for the carries, 1 mark for saying twice.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: 5a + 6. When a = 4, 5 × 4 + 6 = 26.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 5a, 1 mark for 6, 1 mark for replacing a, 1 mark for 26.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3 × 8 = 24, 8 × 3 = 24, 24 ÷ 3 = 8, 24 ÷ 8 = 3
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct fact.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 1/4 kg
   Working / marking points: Wholes 2 + 1 = 3 (1 mark); parts 2/4 + 3/4 = 5/4 = 1 1/4 (1 mark); total 4 1/4 kg (1 mark).

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.45, 0.06 and 0.7
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct decimal.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: 7/3 and 11/6
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 2 × 3 + 1 = 7 so 7/3; 2 marks for 1 × 6 + 5 = 11 so 11/6.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Area is the amount of flat surface a shape covers, in square units. Volume is the amount of space a solid takes up, in cubic units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for area and 1 mark for volume.
